title: Opening any 4.x 32-bit Editor prevents 64-bit Editors from launching.
body:
### Tested versions

- Initially discovered in 4.5.1
- Reproducible in 4.x versions including the latest 4.6 snapshot. It happens on both mono and non-mono.

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 256V (8 threads) - 15.54 GiB memory

### Issue description

Opening the 32-bit editor will prevent the 64-bit editor from opening.
```================================================================
CrashHandlerException: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.mono.official (f62fdbde15035c5576dad93e586201f4d41ef0cb)
Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues
[1] error(-1): no debug info in PE/COFF executable
[2] error(-1): no debug info in PE/COFF executable
... (I've edited out [3] ~ [27] since they were also duplicates.)
[28] error(-1): no debug info in PE/COFF executable
-- END OF C++ BACKTRACE --
===================================
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the **64-bit** version of Godot (Any version), and close it.
2. Open the **32-bit** version of Godot (Any version), and close it. 
3. Re-open the **64-bit** version again, and the crash happens.

### Steps to fix the issue
**Option A**
_This method fixes the problem until it's reproduced via the steps above._
1. Open the folder that contains Godot's editor data.
2. Delete the shader cache folder.

**Option B**
_This method fixes the problem, but you must always launch Godot via command line._
1. Launch the 64-bit editor via commandline with any rendering method other than gl_compatibility.
Ex: `Godot_v4.5.1-stable_mono_win64.exe --rendering-method forward_plus`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

n/a
